decision.justification: Two independent views of this merchant disagree with its declaration. The storefront presents a different business, and the infrastructure channel agrees. Neither could have produced the other: a merchant cannot change its payment behaviour without changing its actual business, and cannot change its interface without changing what customers see.
notes: The corroborating view is infrastructure rather than telemetry. This is the rented-account shape: the genuine store keeps trading, so the payment mixture stays near the category baseline and telemetry alone never crosses its threshold.

attribution.label: Volume trend slope (vs category)
attribution.explains: Fitted daily growth rate of transaction count.

attribution.label: Peak-to-median volume ratio (vs category)
attribution.explains: Largest single day relative to the median day.

attribution.label: Round-value share drift (vs category)
attribution.explains: Recent minus prior window. Separates a merchant that has always priced in round numbers from one that started last month.

attribution.label: Post-peak persistence (vs category)
attribution.explains: Volume after the peak divided by volume before it. Near 1.0 means a spike that decayed -- a sale. Well above 1.0 means a step change that held.

narrative.text: Merchant MID100032 declared digital_services at onboarding 641 days ago. Telemetry agrees: the largest deviations from the digital_services baseline are slope_log_volume at +5.4 sigma (observed 0.013 against a category baseline of 0.00251), peak_ratio at +2.0 sigma (observed 1.95 against a category baseline of 1.57), chargeback_drift at -1.9 sigma (observed -0.0066 against a category baseline of 0). The checkout surface presents a crypto_exchange interface at 0.93 confidence, against a declared category of digital_services. This vertical cannot be approved on this platform. Linked to 6 other merchants by rare shared asn, beneficiary id, device fp, ip block, payout fingerprint, phone fp, script bundle. Their payment behaviour is also moving in step (synchrony 0.52), which independent businesses do not do. It is linked to 6 other merchant accounts by rare shared asn, beneficiary id, device fp, ip block, payout fingerprint, phone fp, script bundle, and those accounts are moving in step (synchrony 0.52). In total 2 independent views of this merchant contradict its declaration. The investigation used 4 of a permitted 8 steps and stopped because confidence threshold met. Recommended tier restricts settlements, corroborated by the infrastructure channel; the storefront alone would not have been sufficient.
